alg-threshold-partial-pivot-sparse-lu:
## Definition

Input a nonsingular real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, an initial simultaneous row-and-column permutation matrix $P$ under the row-action convention of [[def-permutation-matrix-partial-pivoting-and-pivot-growth]], and a threshold $\theta\in(0,1]$. Start from $S^{(0)}=PAP^T$. Maintain a row permutation $Q$, a unit lower-triangular factor $L$, and the current active matrix. Every real scalar operation uses [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]; if an exact intermediate is nonzero and subnormal, overflows, or the operation reports range failure, return **range-failure** at its stage. The pivot tests and tie-breaking comparisons are exact guards on the current stored values. For $k=0,\ldots,n-1$, ties for a maximum are resolved by choosing the smallest current row index.

At stage $k$, let $m_k=\max_{i\ge k}|S^{(k)}_{ik}|$. If $m_k=0$, return **singular-pivot**$(k)$. If $|S^{(k)}_{kk}|\ge\theta m_k$, select row $p=k$; otherwise select a row $p$ attaining $m_k$. Swap rows $p$ and $k$ of the active matrix and the already stored entries of those rows of $L$, and record the swap in $Q$. If the selected pivot is zero, return **singular-pivot**$(k)$.

For each $i>k$ with a currently stored or newly generated entry in column $k$, compute $l_{ik}=S^{(k)}_{ik}/S^{(k)}_{kk}$ and update each active entry by
$$S^{(k+1)}_{ij}=S^{(k)}_{ij}-l_{ik}S^{(k)}_{kj},\qquad i,j>k.$$
Allocate any position whose update is nonzero; this is numerical fill. If an arithmetic operation is not representable or reports a range error, return **range-failure**$(k)$. Continue until $k=n$. On success return $(Q,P,L,U)$, where the row and initial symmetric permutations are explicit. The procedure makes no claim of a universal fill or growth bound.
def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter:
## Definition

Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ satisfy $A=A^*$, where $A^*=\overline A^{\,T}$. Define a real symmetric pattern matrix $H\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$ by $H_{ii}=0$ and, for $i<j$, set $H_{ij}=H_{ji}=1$ exactly when $A_{ij}\ne0$; otherwise set both entries to zero. Since $A_{ji}=\overline{A_{ij}}$, this pattern records exactly the undirected off-diagonal support of $A$.

Apply the graph and elimination-ordering convention of [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]] to $H$. Its structural graph is the **Hermitian structural graph** of $A$, and its filled graphs are the symbolic pattern used for Hermitian elimination. The real matrix $H$ records only support; numerical Schur complements are formed from $A$.
alg-nested-dissection-ordering-on-regula:
## Definition

Input an integer $k\ge1$ and dimension $d\in\{2,3\}$. The coordinate vertices are $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}^d$. Identify them with the zero-based matrix indices $0,\ldots,k^d-1$ by the lexicographic bijection $q(i_1,\ldots,i_d)=\sum_{a=1}^d i_a k^{d-a}$. The grid graph has an edge between two coordinate vertices exactly when they differ by $1$ in one coordinate and agree in all others. Use the graph and ordering conventions of [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]] on these indices. Thus $d=2$ gives the five-point graph and $d=3$ the seven-point graph.

Order a rectangular coordinate subbox recursively as follows. For each coordinate whose side length is at least $2$, choose its lower median coordinate, namely the coordinate with $\lfloor(m-1)/2\rfloor$ positions below it in a side of length $m$. Let $S$ be the union of the coordinate hyperplanes at those selected medians. Delete $S$, obtaining at most $2^d$ nonempty rectangular child boxes. Recursively order the child boxes in lexicographic order of their lower corners, then append the vertices of $S$ in lexicographic order. If no coordinate has side length at least $2$, append the remaining vertex as a terminal separator. Apply this rule first to the whole grid. The resulting order is the **coordinate nested-dissection ordering**.

The recursion uses only the graph geometry. It makes no fill or complexity claim for arbitrary graphs.
lem-filled-edge-path-characterisation:
## Statement

Use the zero-based graph and ordering of [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]]. For distinct remaining vertices $x,y\in V_k$, the pair $\{x,y\}$ is an edge of $G_k$ if and only if the original graph $G_0$ contains a finite walk from $x$ to $y$ all of whose internal vertices belong to $\{v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}\}$. A walk may repeat vertices; its internal vertices are the entries other than its two endpoints.
thm-threshold-sparse-lu-residual-with-gr:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be nonsingular, $n\ge1$, and run [[alg-threshold-partial-pivot-sparse-lu]] with $\theta\in(0,1]$. Assume a successful run under the real operation model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], with unit roundoff $u<1$ and every exact intermediate either zero or normal. Let $M=\max_{i,j}|a_{ij}|>0$, let $S^{(k)}$ be the active matrix at stage $k$ including its current pivot row, and define the actual growth of this run by
$$
\rho=\frac{\max_{k,i,j}|S^{(k)}_{ij}|}{M}\ge1.
$$
For its computed factors and accumulated row permutation, there is a residual $\Delta A$ such that
$$
\widehat QPA P^T+\Delta A=\widehat L\widehat U,
\qquad
\max_{i,j}|\Delta A_{ij}|\le \frac{8nu}{\theta}\rho M,
\qquad
\|\Delta A\|_\infty\le \frac{8n^2u}{\theta}\rho M,
\qquad \|X\|_\infty:=\max_i\sum_j|X_{ij}|.
$$
The bound retains this run's actual growth $\rho$ and makes no uniform small-growth claim. This residual theorem is for real arithmetic; the local operation model used here does not specify a general complex division primitive.
def-elimination-tree-and-column-reach:
## Definition

Let $A=A^*$ and use the Hermitian structural graph of [[def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter]]. The graph definition [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]] supplies the ordering $v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1}$, filled graphs, parent map, and elimination forest. For each $k$, let $N_k(v_k)$ be the later-neighbor set at elimination of $v_k$, and define its structural column set
$$\mathcal C_k=\{v_k\}\cup N_k(v_k).$$
Its off-diagonal size is the column count $\ell_k=|N_k(v_k)|$. An **ancestor** of $v_k$ is obtained by following one or more supplied parent edges; a **descendant** is the inverse relation. The **reach** of $v_k$ is the set of vertices visited by following its parent path, including $v_k$.
lem-nested-dissection-fronts-are-boundar:
## Statement

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and use the coordinate grid and recursive ordering of [[alg-nested-dissection-ordering-on-regular-grids]]. For a recursion box $B$, let $S_B$ be its median separator; for the terminal one-vertex box take $S_B=B$. Let $\partial^+B$ be the set of grid vertices outside $B$ adjacent to some vertex of $B$. If $v\in S_B$, then every later filled neighbor of $v$ lies in $S_B\cup\partial^+B$. If every side of $B$ has length at most $s$, then
$$
|\{v\}\cup N^+_\pi(v)|\le |S_B|+|\partial^+B|\le 3d\,s^{d-1}.
$$
lem-hermitian-schur-support-is-contained:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ be Hermitian and use the Hermitian structural graph adapter of [[def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter]]. Fix an ordering and suppose each scalar pivot $p_k=S^k_{v_kv_k}$ is nonzero. Form the Hermitian Schur updates
$$S^{k+1}_{ij}=S^k_{ij}-S^k_{iv_k}p_k^{-1}S^k_{v_kj}.$$
Then every $S^k$ is Hermitian, every nonzero off-diagonal entry of $S^k$ is an edge of the corresponding filled graph, and the later neighbors of every eliminated vertex form a clique in the next filled graph.
alg-symmetric-indefinite-block-ldl-star:
## Definition

The exact-arithmetic branch is specified first; the finite-precision branch below implements the same declared pivots by certified real-component kernels. Input a Hermitian $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, an ordering $\pi=(v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1})$ and its simultaneous permutation matrix $P$ in the convention of [[def-permutation-matrix-partial-pivoting-and-pivot-growth]], an ordered partition of the permuted positions into consecutive blocks of size $1$ or $2$, and a threshold $\theta\in(0,1]$. Apply $P$ once and maintain the Hermitian active Schur complement of $B=PAP^*$. Form the structural graph from [[def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter]], then relabel its vertex $v_i$ by ordered position $i$; use the graph and fill convention of [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]] on this position-labeled graph. At stage $r$, the next declared block is the leading active block. For a $1\times1$ block at index $t$, require $d=a_{tt}\ne0$ and
$$\max_{i\ne t,\ i\text{ active}}|a_{it}|\le\theta^{-1}|d|.$$
For a declared $2\times2$ pair $(s,t)$, form the Hermitian principal block
$$D=\begin{pmatrix}a_{ss}&a_{st}\\\overline{a_{st}}&a_{tt}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Require $\det D\ne0$, and let $c_1=\max_{i\notin\{s,t\}}|a_{is}|$ and $c_2=\max_{i\notin\{s,t\}}|a_{it}|$, with an empty maximum equal to zero. Accept the pair only if
$$|D^{-1}|\begin{pmatrix}c_1\\c_2\end{pmatrix}
\le\theta^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\end{pmatrix}$$
componentwise. If the declared block fails its test, return **pivot-failure**$(r)$.

Write the active matrix as
$$\begin{pmatrix}D&B^*\\B&C\end{pmatrix}.$$
Compute the block multiplier $M=BD^{-1}$ and the trailing update $C-BD^{-1}B^*$, retaining all positions allowed by the symbolic graph even when their current numerical value is zero. Symbolically, for the pivot-block index set $J$, let $N(J)$ be the union of its active graph neighbors; remove $J$ and connect every pair of distinct vertices in $N(J)$. Store $D$ as the next diagonal block and continue on the trailing matrix. On completion return $(P,L,D_{\rm blk})$, where $L$ is unit lower block-triangular and $D_{\rm blk}$ is block diagonal. The method may return **pivot-failure**$(r)$ on a nonsingular input when the declared pivot sequence contains a block that fails its test; it asserts no universal growth bound.

In the finite-precision branch, at each declared block use [[alg-certified-hermitian-one-and-two-by-two-ldl-kernel]] with the same threshold, permutation and symbolic block-neighbor clique. Store its returned $D_r,\widehat M_r$ in $D_{\rm blk},\widehat L$, and continue on its Hermitian $\widehat S_{r+1}$. Return `range-failure`, `pivot-failure` or `pivot-inconclusive` with stage index and partial factors as specified by the kernel. A successful run returns $(P,\widehat L,D_{\rm blk})$ together with its pivot certificates. Exact test semantics are retained: only certified admissible blocks are accepted; an unresolved determinant or threshold is inconclusive. No general complex division, automatic pivot existence or universal factor-growth guarantee is assumed.
lem-elimination-tree-reach-contains-each:
## Statement

Let $v_k$ be a vertex in the elimination forest supplied by [[def-elimination-tree-and-column-reach]]. Every later filled neighbor of $v_k$ lies on its parent path and is therefore an ancestor. Consequently, if $v_s$ is a child of $v_k$, then every later neighbor of $v_s$ other than $v_k$ is a later neighbor of $v_k$; equivalently,
$$\mathcal C_s\setminus\{v_s\}\subseteq\mathcal C_k.$$
alg-sparse-cholesky-with-invalid-pivot-s:
## Definition

Input a Hermitian positive-definite $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ in the convention of [[def-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal]], its Hermitian structural graph from [[def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter]], and an ordering $\pi=(v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1})$. Use the operation model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Let $P$ be the permutation matrix whose row $j$ is row $v_j$ of $I_n$, so the ordered matrix is $B=PAP^*$ and $B_{ij}=A_{v_i v_j}$. Relabel the filled graph on the original vertices by positions: $\{i,j\}\in E^+_\pi$ exactly when $\{v_i,v_j\}$ is an edge of the filled graph. In every displayed sum, accumulate in increasing $k$ from left to right.

Preallocate only the diagonal and lower-triangular positions permitted by $E^+_\pi$. The support guarantee for complex Hermitian Schur complements is proved in [[lem-hermitian-schur-support-is-contained-in-structural-fill]]. Initialize those positions from the lower triangle of $B$, using zero where a position is not present in the original pattern. For $j=0,\ldots,n-1$, perform these instructions:

1. Compute $d_j=B_{jj}-\sum_{k<j}l_{jk}\overline{l_{jk}}$ using only already computed entries, with an empty sum equal to zero. If an operation reports range failure, return **range-failure**$(j)$. If $d_j$ is not a finite positive real number, return **invalid-pivot**$(j,d_j)$.
2. Set $l_{jj}=\sqrt{d_j}$. If the square root is not finite and positive, return **range-failure**$(j)$.
3. For each $i>j$ such that $\{i,j\}\in E^+_\pi$, compute
$$l_{ij}=\frac{B_{ij}-\sum_{k<j}l_{ik}\overline{l_{jk}}}{l_{jj}}.$$
If an operation reports range failure, return **range-failure**$(j)$. Set structurally absent entries to zero.

If all columns finish, return **success**$(P,L)$. In exact arithmetic, the intended factor convention is $PAP^*=LL^*$ with $L$ lower triangular and positive real diagonal. The finite-arithmetic procedure makes no claim that every positive-definite input returns success: a rounded pivot can fail the stated test.
thm-block-ldl-star-residual-with-actual-:
## Statement

Consider a successful run of [[alg-symmetric-indefinite-block-ldl-star]] on a Hermitian input with its declared permutation $P$ and fixed pivot-block sequence. In every formula, $\|X\|_2$ is the operator norm induced by the Euclidean inner products. At stage $r$, write the active matrix as
$$\begin{pmatrix}D_r&B_r^*\\B_r&C_r\end{pmatrix}.$$
Suppose the computed trailing block is
$$\widehat S_{r+1}=C_r-B_rD_r^{-1}B_r^*+\Delta_r,$$
where $\Delta_r$ is the exact local update residual. Embed it into the full permuted coordinates as $E_r$, with zeros on all previously eliminated and current pivot indices. Let $T_r$ be the $n\times n$ identity on previously eliminated coordinates and the padded unit lower block elimination matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\B_rD_r^{-1}&I\end{pmatrix}$$
on the current pivot and trailing coordinates. Set $W_1=I$ and $W_r=T_1\cdots T_{r-1}$ for $r>1$. Then
$$\|PAP^*-L_{\rm ex}D_{\rm blk}L_{\rm ex}^*\|_2
\le\sum_r\|W_r\|_2^2\|\Delta_r\|_2
\le\rho_{\rm blk}\sum_r\eta_r\bigl(\|C_r\|_2+\|B_r\|_2^2\|D_r^{-1}\|_2\bigr),$$
provided the actual local residuals satisfy
$$\|\Delta_r\|_2\le\eta_r\bigl(\|C_r\|_2+\|B_r\|_2^2\|D_r^{-1}\|_2\bigr).$$
Here $L_{\rm ex}$ is the product of the exact-multiplier transformations $T_r$, not a rounded stored multiplier factor. Here $\rho_{\rm blk}:=\max_r\|W_r\|_2^2$ is the actual amplification from this pivot sequence. The trailing-only statement is conditional in this general form. For the specified kernel, [[lem-hermitian-block-ldl-kernel-roundoff-and-reconstruction-residual]] proves it with $\eta_r=\eta_{k_r,t_r}$, retaining the actual normalized-determinant and range certificates. It makes no uniform smallness claim for $\rho_{\rm blk}$, $\|D_r^{-1}\|_2$, or $\eta_r$.

In exact arithmetic every accepted block is nonsingular and each update has $\Delta_r=0$, so a successful run returns $PAP^*=LD_{\rm blk}L^*$.

For the actual rounded output use $\widehat T_r$ built from stored $\widehat M_r$, its full reconstruction residual $F_r$ from the local kernel lemma, and padded products $\widehat W_r=\widehat T_1\cdots\widehat T_{r-1}$. Then
$$PAP^*-\widehat LD_{\rm blk}\widehat L^*=\sum_r\widehat W_rF_r\widehat W_r^*,\qquad \|PAP^*-\widehat LD_{\rm blk}\widehat L^*\|_2\le\sum_r\|\widehat W_r\|_2^2 f_r\le\widehat\rho_{\rm blk}\sum_r f_r,$$
where $f_r$ is the proved explicit local bound and $\widehat\rho_{\rm blk}=\max_r\|\widehat W_r\|_2^2$. This includes multiplier coupling residuals as well as trailing updates. Neither actual growth nor inverse-pivot conditioning is assumed uniformly small.
thm-sparse-cholesky-structural-pattern-w:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ be Hermitian positive definite and use its pattern from [[def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter]]. The local Hermitian Schur-support lemma [[lem-hermitian-schur-support-is-contained-in-structural-fill]] applies. In exact arithmetic, the Cholesky recurrence in [[alg-sparse-cholesky-with-invalid-pivot-status]] returns the unique factor $L$ satisfying $PAP^*=LL^*$ and positive diagonal, and every nonzero strict-lower entry of $L$ is permitted by the filled graph $G^+_\pi$.

For $i>j$ with $\{i,j\}\in E^+_\pi$ (where ordered position $i$ represents original vertex $v_i$), define the recurrence numerator
$$\nu_{ij}=B_{ij}-\sum_{k<j}l_{ik}\overline{l_{jk}},\qquad B=PAP^*.$$
If $\nu_{ij}\ne0$ at every permitted strict-lower position, then the numerical nonzero pattern of $L$ is exactly the lower-triangular part of $G^+_\pi$ together with its diagonal. Without this no-cancellation hypothesis only the upper-pattern inclusion is asserted.
alg-multifrontal-cholesky-and-sparse-tri:
## Definition

Input a Hermitian positive-definite matrix $A$, its Hermitian structural graph from [[def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter]], and an ordering $\pi=(v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1})$. Let $P$ be the permutation matrix whose row $r$ is row $v_r$ of $I_n$, and put $B=PAP^*$. Use the filled graph and parent forest of [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]] and the column patterns of [[def-elimination-tree-and-column-reach]]. For each original vertex $v_r$, let its front index set be
$$F_r=\{v_r\}\cup N_r^+,$$
where $N_r^+$ is its later-neighbor set in the filled graph. Assign each original matrix entry $A_{pq}$ to the front of the endpoint eliminated first (to their common endpoint for a diagonal entry).

Process the elimination forest from leaves to roots. At front $r$, initialize a dense Hermitian array indexed by $F_r$ with the entries assigned to $v_r$. For each child $s$, add its stored contribution array to the entries whose indices lie in $F_s\setminus\{v_s\}$, using the common original-vertex labels. The inclusion needed for this addition is supplied by [[lem-elimination-tree-reach-contains-each-filled-neighbor]]. Apply the pivot, range, and invalid-pivot instructions of [[alg-sparse-cholesky-with-invalid-pivot-status]] to the scalar pivot $v_r$: store factor entries $L_{q r}$ for later vertices $v_q$ in the front and replace the trailing front block $C$ by its Schur update $C-bb^*/d$. Send this trailing contribution array to the parent; at a root discard only the empty final remainder. A failed pivot or range operation returns the same indexed status and stops the factorization.

For a successful factor $L$, a solve with right-hand side $b$ uses these instructions:

1. Set $x=Pb$.
2. For $j=0,\ldots,n-1$, divide $x_j$ by $l_{jj}$, then for every stored $l_{ij}$ with $i>j$ set $x_i\leftarrow x_i-l_{ij}x_j$.
3. For $j=n-1,\ldots,0$, set $x_j\leftarrow (x_j-\sum_{i>j}\overline{l_{ij}}x_i)/\overline{l_{jj}}$, using the backward-substitution convention of [[def-forward-and-back-substitution-for-triangular-systems]].
4. Return $P^*x$.

The factorization returns either $(P,L)$ or a pivot/range status. The solve returns the unique solution of $Az=b$ only after successful factorization; no finite-precision error guarantee is part of this procedure definition.
thm-multifrontal-elimination-equivalence:
## Statement

Assume exact arithmetic, a Hermitian positive-definite $A$, and a successful ordered factorization using [[alg-multifrontal-cholesky-and-sparse-triangular-solves]]. The fronts and contribution arrays give the same Cholesky factor as scalar elimination in ordering $\pi$. With $d_r=\ell_r+1=|F_r|$, the arithmetic work for assembly and scalar front updates is
$$O\!\left(\sum_{r=1}^n d_r^2\right),$$
the symbolic factor allocation has exactly $\sum_{r=1}^n d_r$ positions, and each forward/back substitution solve uses $O(\sum_r d_r)$ scalar operations. These are arithmetic and factor-storage counts; they are not wall-clock or total workspace bounds.
thm-nested-dissection-grid-work-and-stor:
## Statement

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, $k\ge2$, and $n=k^d$. Identify the coordinate grid $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}^d$ with the zero-based matrix indices by the lexicographic bijection in [[alg-nested-dissection-ordering-on-regular-grids]]. Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite, with structural graph a subgraph of the $d$-dimensional nearest-neighbor grid. Under the coordinate nested-dissection ordering, exact scalar multifrontal Cholesky has
$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
d&\text{arithmetic work}&\text{symbolic factor storage}\\
2&O(n^{3/2})&O(n\log n)\\
3&O(n^2)&O(n^{4/3}).
\end{array}
$$
The storage is the number of allocated factor entries, including structural zeros, and excludes temporary contribution arrays. The bounds use the stated grid geometry; they assert no general-graph bound. For $k=1$, there is one pivot and both work and factor storage are $O(1)$.
alg-certified-hermitian-one-and-two-by-t:
## Definition

Input stored Hermitian $D\in\mathbb C^{k\times k}$, $B\in\mathbb C^{t\times k}$ and $C\in\mathbb C^{t\times t}$, with $k\in\{1,2\}$, $t\ge0$, threshold $0<\theta\le1$, unit roundoff $0<u<1$, and a finite certificate budget. Use [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Divide complex values by a nonzero real denominator by separately dividing their real and imaginary components, using the model's real operations; no complex division is used. Any invalid operation, nonfinite output or nonzero exact intermediate outside the normal range returns `range-failure`. Hermitian counterparts, sign changes and conjugation are exact copies.

The pivot controller uses exact real-RAM arithmetic on the stored real components and the supplied exact $u,\theta$, separately from the rounded numerical kernel. Its allowed operations are real addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a certified nonzero real denominator, fixed nonnegative integer powers, and comparisons. Each field operation or comparison consumes one unit of the nonnegative integer controller budget; a fixed power is expanded into its stated finite chain of multiplications. Before any controller operation, if no unit remains, return `pivot-inconclusive`. Exact sign/absolute-value and maximum decisions use comparisons and conditional sign changes. For binary/rational stored values and rational $u,\theta$, exact rational arithmetic implements this controller with finite integers; no bit-complexity bound is claimed. There is no optional unspecified certifier or sign oracle. For complex modulus guards, a successful two-component scaled norm first scales by the larger absolute real component, then rounds both divisions, squares, sum, positive square root and rescaling. Its returned $h$ gives bounds $h/(1+u)^4\le|z|\le h/(1-u)^4$; zero is exact. Maxima use the corresponding lower/upper bounds and an empty maximum is zero. Evaluate modulus guards once per distinct stored complex value in row-major order, using only the displayed rounded scaled norm; its finite floating operations carry their own range status. No exact square root or additional modulus operation is used by the controller. Evaluate each displayed rational bound left to right, entrywise in row-major order; evaluate column maxima in increasing row order, then the at-most-two-term matrix-vector bounds in increasing column order, and finally the acceptance comparisons in row order. Compute each of $(1-u)^4,(1+u)^4,(1+u)^5$ by left-associated repeated multiplication. These prescribed finite expression trees and finite input loops fix the guard procedure and its budget count. If acceptance is not established, evaluate the stated lower-bound failure comparisons; if neither conclusion follows, return `pivot-inconclusive` without refinement.

For $k=1$, write $D=[d]$, $d$ real. If $d=0$ return `pivot-failure`. Certify $\max_i|B_{i1}|\le|d|/\theta$ using the guard bounds. A rigorous lower maximum exceeding $|d|/\theta$ returns `pivot-failure`; an unresolved comparison returns `pivot-inconclusive`. Set $\widehat M_{i1}$ by rounded real-component divisions of $B_{i1}$ by $d$.

For $k=2$, write $D=\begin{pmatrix}a&z\\\overline z&c\end{pmatrix}$ with real $a,c$, and set $s=\max(|a|,|c|,|\operatorname{Re}z|,|\operatorname{Im}z|)$. If $s=0$ return `pivot-failure`. Compute the four real entries of $\widehat E=\operatorname{fl}(D/s)$ and the conjugate counterpart by copying. In order compute
$$p=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat a\widehat c),\quad q_1=\operatorname{fl}((\operatorname{Re}\widehat z)^2),\quad q_2=\operatorname{fl}((\operatorname{Im}\widehat z)^2),\quad q=\operatorname{fl}(q_1+q_2),\quad \widehat d=\operatorname{fl}(p-q).$$
Put $\epsilon_d=3((1+u)^5-1)$ and $\widehat J=\operatorname{adj}(\widehat E)=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat c&-\widehat z\\-\overline{\widehat z}&\widehat a\end{pmatrix}$ by copies. Unless $|\widehat d|>\epsilon_d$ is certified, return `pivot-inconclusive`. For each entry obtain rigorous modulus bounds $j^-_{ij}\le|\widehat J_{ij}|\le j^+_{ij}$ and set
$$U_{ij}=\frac{j^+_{ij}}{s(1-u)(|\widehat d|-\epsilon_d)},\qquad V_{ij}=\frac{j^-_{ij}}{s(1+u)(|\widehat d|+\epsilon_d)}.$$
Let $c_j^-,c_j^+$ bound $\max_i|B_{ij}|$. Accept only if $U c^+\le\theta^{-1}(1,1)^T$ componentwise. If any coordinate of $V c^-$ exceeds $\theta^{-1}$ return `pivot-failure`; otherwise an unresolved test returns `pivot-inconclusive`. On acceptance compute $\widehat B_s=\operatorname{fl}(B/s)$, $K=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat B_s\widehat J)$ by sequential two-term complex dots, then $\widehat M=\operatorname{fl}(K/\widehat d)$ by real-component divisions. No explicit reciprocal $1/s$ is formed.

For either block size, compute each allocated lower-triangle entry of $\widehat Z=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat M B^*)$ by sequential $k$-term dots. Compute $\operatorname{fl}(C-\widehat Z)$ there, retain only its real component on the diagonal, and obtain upper entries by exact conjugation. Return `success` with stored $D,\widehat M,\widehat S$ and the pivot certificates. An empty trailing block returns empty $\widehat M,\widehat S$. In the sparse application, allocate the original block-neighbor clique and retain positions even when their numerical value is zero. Additional sparsity drops must be recorded separately as additive perturbations.
lem-hermitian-block-ldl-kernel-roundoff-:
## Statement

For a successful [[alg-certified-hermitian-one-and-two-by-two-ldl-kernel]], let $k\in\{1,2\}$ and $t$ be its trailing dimension. Every accepted $D$ is nonsingular and satisfies the original exact componentwise threshold test. For either size put $g_j=(1+6u)/(1-(j-1)u)-1$ for $j=1,2$. For $k=1$ put $\omega_1=u$. For $k=2$ put
$$\mu=\frac{\epsilon_d}{|\widehat d|}<1,\quad \nu=\sqrt2u(1+\mu)+\mu,$$
$$\chi=u+(1+u)(\sqrt2g_2(1+u)+u),\qquad \omega_2=\nu+\chi(1+\nu).$$
For either size define
$$q_k=(1+u)(1+g_k)(1+\omega_k)-1,\quad e_M=\omega_k\|B\|_F\|D^{-1}\|_2,$$
$$\beta=\sqrt2\bigl(u\|C\|_F+q_k\|B\|_F^2\|D^{-1}\|_2\bigr),\qquad \eta_{k,t}=\sqrt2\max\{u\sqrt t,kq_k\}.$$
Then, writing $M=BD^{-1}$ and $\Delta=\widehat S-(C-BD^{-1}B^*)$,
$$\|\widehat M-M\|_F\le e_M,\qquad \|\Delta\|_2\le\beta\le\eta_{k,t}(\|C\|_2+\|B\|_2^2\|D^{-1}\|_2).$$
For $t=0$ all residuals are zero and use $e_M=\beta=\eta_{k,0}=0$. The coefficients are explicit unit-roundoff bounds, $O(u)$ at fixed nonzero normalized determinant as $u\to0$; near-singular scaled pivots have no uniform smallness guarantee.

The actual stored multipliers also have coupling residual $N=\widehat MD-B$. Set $\widehat T=\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\\widehat M&I\end{pmatrix}$. The full reconstruction residual satisfies
$$F=\begin{pmatrix}D&B^*\\B&C\end{pmatrix}-\widehat T\operatorname{diag}(D,\widehat S)\widehat T^*=\begin{pmatrix}0&-N^*\\-N&-\Delta-(\widehat M-M)B^*-\widehat MN^*\end{pmatrix},$$
$$\|F\|_2\le f:=\beta+e_M\|B\|_2+(1+\|\widehat M\|_2)e_M\|D\|_2.$$
This additional residual is necessary for actual rounded output factors; the trailing-only residual applies to conceptual exact multipliers.
